newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares end quiet ahead of ITC results.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares end quiet ahead of ITC results.

text.p: Bombay shares ended flat in featureless trade on Tuesday as traders awaited full-year results of tobacco conglomerate ITC.
"The market was absolutely range bound," said Sanjeev Choithani, chief dealer at brokers Pashupati Advani.
"There was some speculative squaring up in ITC, but overall it was a very dull day."

ITC, one of India's top 10 private companies is expected to announce results for fiscal 1996/97 (April-March) at about 1700 hours (1130 GMT). Analysts expect ITC to unveil net profit of about 3.4 billion rupees to 4.0 billion from 2.61 billion last year.
The 1996/97 profits will reflect the strong margins in tobacco and cigarette sales, analysts said.
"We expect the results to be extremely good," said K. Ramachandran, analyst at Birla Marlin Securities. "We are forecasting a net profit of 3.98 billion rupees."
He saw cigarette volume sales growth of 10 percent and margins rising 7.0 percent.

Profit in 1995/96 had fallen to 2.61 billion rupees from 2.62 billion the year before, due to loss-making deals in farm products and global trade. Britain's BAT Industries Plc hold 31.7 percent equity in ITC.
Some traders said the weak performance of ITC on Tuesday might be indicative of a lacklustre performance.
"People have already discounted the results. Only a bonus or rights issue might perhaps buoy market sentiment," said Pashupati Advani's Choithani.
ITC shares ended 9.0 rupees lower at 439.50 amid volumes of over 4.6 million shares. The stock was off 453.50, the day's intra-day high.
HDFC Bank shares rose rose to 62.50 rupees, but ended with a net gain of 1.0 rupee at 60.25 after the firm posted a 100 percent rise in its 1996/97 net profit to 405 million rupees.
